title: Mouse Without Borders: with "Use Service" enabled, SYSTEM instances start but never open TCP 15100/15101

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplies a current reproduction, a tested Connect workaround, and a code-level explanation. Pinned source confirms service-mode DPAPI key handling and that toggling UseService saves the setting without an evident key migration; safe transition behavior needs design review.
evidence: The reporter reproduced on 0.102.3101 and describes a per-user install with Use Service enabled.
After the transition the service instances have no TCP listeners until Connect is completed with the existing key.
The reporter tested Connect as a workaround; it restored listeners within about a second.
The latest issue comment includes a numbered setup, observed missing listeners, tested recovery, and a proposed security-preserving transition.

The codec encrypts service-mode keys using the SYSTEM identity and rejects values without the expected encrypted prefix. UseService persists the mode setting; the pairing-key codec is selected for the executing identity. judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce the issue-specific scenario: Make service-mode pairing-key transition explicit and recoverable

fix_assessment.rationale: The issue is well grounded, but migration must preserve the service-mode security boundary and must not silently expose a key to standard users.

proposed_fixes.title: Make service-mode pairing-key transition explicit and recoverable
proposed_fixes.root_cause: When service mode uses the SYSTEM-bound DPAPI codec, an existing normal-mode plaintext pairing key is not readable by the service instance. Toggling UseService alone can leave it without a usable key, so it opens no pairing sockets until Connect supplies a valid key.
plan: Keep the SYSTEM identity protection boundary; never silently accept a normal-user plaintext key in the secure-desktop service.
Add an explicit, permission-checked pairing transition that lets the service re-encrypt an existing key when authorized, and make the unavailable-key state visible in Settings.
Ensure the service does not install input hooks or allow switching when no usable pairing key is configured; add tests for both service-mode transitions.
verification: Pair normally, enable Use Service as an administrator, restart, and verify the service listens on 15100/15101 with the existing key.
Disable service mode and verify the inverse transition is explicit and recoverable.
A non-elevated toggle cannot silently transfer a plaintext user key into the secure-desktop service.

information_gaps.information: Whether disabling Use Service and restarting restores the pre-existing normal-mode pairing without pressing Connect, after the service-mode failure has been observed.
information_gaps.why_needed: This verifies whether the key transition is one-way or whether the service mode simply lacks a usable key while enabled.

actions.label: Make service-mode pairing-key transition explicit and recoverable

reproduce.title: Make service-mode pairing-key transition explicit and recoverable
prerequisites: Two or more Windows PCs with Mouse Without Borders paired in normal mode.
An administrator-capable test machine; do not use a production secure-desktop setup.
setup: Confirm normal-mode peers connect before changing the service option.
steps: Run PowerToys as administrator and enable Use Service on one paired machine.
Restart PowerToys and wait three minutes.
Check whether TCP 15100/15101 are listening and whether the peer remains paired.
Use Connect with the existing key and verify whether listeners and connectivity recover.
reproduce.expected_result: The current key remains usable through an authorized transition, or Settings clearly requests the required pairing action without silently losing local input.

comment.body: Thanks for the detailed service-mode reproduction and the Connect workaround. After observing the missing listeners with Use Service enabled, could you disable Use Service and restart without pressing Connect, then confirm whether the original normal-mode pairing returns? This distinguishes a service-only key incompatibility from a pairing state that is lost across the transition.

actions.label: Approve lightweight direction: Make service-mode pairing-key transition explicit and recoverable
